decisions.reason: It serves the growing but still niche particle-therapy segment and, despite a slower commercialization path, it fits the firm's high-end dosimetry portfolio closely enough to justify staying on the market.
A small-volume ionization chamber is a core radiation-measurement product for this firm, so it is likely to be retained unless performance or demand is clearly weak.
This chamber is close to the firm's established expertise and customer base, making continued offering more likely than withdrawal even if volumes are specialized.
A standard clinical ionization chamber line with several models is central to routine radiotherapy QA and therefore likely to remain an anchor product.
Relative dosimetry chambers are standard tools in clinical physics workflows, so dropping such a core product would be unlikely without a clear replacement.
A thimble ionization chamber is a staple product in radiotherapy dosimetry and fits naturally with the firm's calibration, training, and support strengths.
